subject: Pricing & model moves — quick briefing for QBR
messages:
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & model moves — quick briefing for QBR

Team — I pulled together a short briefing for Monday's QBR on two items that'll likely show up in competitive slides: 1) a surprise aggressive price cut from OptiServe (press link below) and 2) a new 7B-30B family release from VeloxAI that they claim is latency-optimized on commodity GPU.

Key bullets (details in attached PDF):
- OptiServe: announced 30% list price reduction on their hosted API for the 7B/13B tiers, effective immediately. Expect PR + partner outreach this week. Implication: potential short-term churn from price-sensitive startups and stronger objections on unit economics.
- VeloxAI: published a new model family "Velox-S" targeted at low-latency egress. Early benchmarks show competitive throughput at 8-bit quant. Might reduce the differentiation of our latency messaging in mid-market pitches.
- GrandTech (prospect): their procurement asked us to re-check pricing comps — attached spreadsheet has our baseline vs. OptiServe/Velox.

Asks: 1) Vivek — recommend a one-slide leader talking point on how we position cost/perf tradeoffs (I drafted one). 2) Maya — any product mitigations to call out (e.g., new caching defaults, batching suggestions, recommended model variants)? 3) Karthik/Laura — can you flag any sales/CS signals to put on the QBR "risk" slide?

Attachments: QBR_competitor_brief_v1.pdf (slide brief), pricing-spreadsheet_velox_optiserve.csv
Links: https://press.optiserve.ai/releases/2026-07-price-cut

Thanks — jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Senior AE, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & model moves — quick briefing for QBR

Thanks Jasmine — solid, concise brief. A couple quick top-line notes for the QBR narrative:
- Signal: Price cuts are tactical and likely targeted at velocity-led segments (SMB/seed-stage). We should call out that our Dedicated and Private customers are less sensitive; emphasize reliability and integration wins.
- Positioning: Advocate "cost predictability" > "cheapest" in the exec slide; show a unit economics example (I can provide a 1-row calc).
- Ask to Maya: include one bullet on "graceful degradation"/fallbacks and the fall-through path when a cheaper model is served by a vendor.

Laura/Karthik: please surface any renewal conversations that could be accelerated by targeted offers (credits/short-term pricing pilots).

Vivek
CEO | Redwood Inference
From: maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & model moves — quick briefing for QBR

Adding product context:
- Velox-S: our early tests show their 13B variant is reasonably fast at 8-bit, but quality drops on instruction-following prompts vs our mid-tier models. We'll call this out as "apparent latency optimization at a quality cost."
- Mitigations we can call in the QBR:
  * Default caching TTL bump for LLM answers where applicable (can reduce token cost by ~12% on average).
  * New suggested routing profile: prefer our quantized 13B internal variant for mid-market probes; keep 30% of traffic on higher-fidelity variants for sensitive features.
  * Quick doc: "When to favor predictions vs. cost" — I'll attach the short one-pager this afternoon.

I'll prep a 1/2-slide on product mitigations + expected unit-econ delta for the QBR package.

— Maya (Product Manager, Serving Runtime)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & model moves — quick briefing for QBR

Thanks — one operational ask: can someone validate the pricing spreadsheet against current committed deals for GrandTech? If procurement is pinging us, we should not respond with a stale comparison. Laura — can you pull the latest commercial terms and flag any concessions we already offered?

Also, for the QBR I'd like a simple chart that shows: "List price vs Effective price after typical discounts" for OptiServe vs Redwood. If anyone has historical churn lift when a competitor made similar moves (2024/2025), include that datapoint.

Karthik
VP, Sales Operations

Great — thanks all for the quick turn. Final plan for Monday's QBR deck:
- 1 slide: Market moves snapshot (OptiServe price cut + Velox-S release) with single-line impact statements. (Vivek to approve framing.)
- 1/2 slide: Product mitigations (Maya to supply) + expected token-cost delta.
- 1 slide: Sales signals & risk (Laura/Karthik to confirm GrandTech status and any active concessions).
- Appendix: full competitor brief + pricing spreadsheet (attached).

I've attached the working brief for the deck (QBR_competitor_brief_v1.pdf). Please flag any factual issues by EOD Monday. If no changes, I'll move this into the QBR folder and share the drive link for the final deck.

Thanks — jasmine
